title: LC-MS/MS Proteomic Data Acquisition
author: Danielle Gutierrez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bs7hnhj6

steps.title: Prepare and Load Samples
steps.instruction: Load and dilute label-free proteomic samples onto EvoTips for processing.

substeps.instruction: Load 1 µL of sample at 1 µg/µL onto EvoTips.
Dilute with 19 µL of mobile phase A (100% water, 0.1% formic acid).
Process samples on tip according to the manufacturer's recommended protocol.

steps.title: Configure LC-MS/MS System
steps.instruction: Set up the Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid mass spectrometer in line with an EvoSep One HPLC system.

substeps.instruction: Place EvoTips onto the EvoSep One.
Install a Dr. Maisch C18 AQ column (100 micron inner diameter, 15 cm long, 3 micron particles, EV1074).

steps.title: Perform Peptide Separation
steps.instruction: Elute samples from EvoTips and separate peptides using the 30 sample per day method settings.

substeps.instruction: Set flow rate to 500 nL/min over a 44 minute gradient.
Use Mobile phase A (100% water, 0.1% formic acid) and Mobile phase B (100% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid).

steps.title: Ionize Peptides
steps.instruction: Ionize eluted peptides using positive mode nanoelectrospray ionization (nESI) with a Nanospray Flex ion source (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Acquire MS Data
steps.instruction: Operate the mass spectrometer using a top 12 data-dependent acquisition mode.

substeps.instruction: Collect Fourier transform mass spectra (FTMS) with 60,000 resolving power, an automated gain control (AGC) target of 1e6, and a maximum injection time of 50 ms over the mass range of 375-1500 m/z.
Filter precursor ions using monoisotopic precursor selection for charge states 2 to 6.
Exclude previously interrogated precursor ions using a 30 s dynamic window (± 10 ppm).

steps.title: Perform Tandem MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Isolate and fragment precursor ions for MS/MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Isolate precursor ions using a 1.2 m/z quadrupole mass filter window.
Fragment ions in the ion-routing multipole via higher energy dissociation (HCD) using a normalized collision energy of 35%.
Acquire ion trap fragmentation spectra using an AGC target of 10,000 and maximum injection time of 60 ms.
Set the first scan mass to 120 m/z to enable detection of the lysine residue fragmented ion.
